segment.why_representative: It is the opening: a human-scale hook (a border town) that zooms out to the thesis, then a puzzle ('the twist'), a historical turn, and the first aphorism. It uses all four layers (map, cartoon, board, archival), the narrator in several placements, a recurring colour-coded pair (north blue / south gold, USA blue / Mexico green), typed captions, counters, a crossing-arrows diagram, a scroll, and two paintings. It does NOT exercise: dialogue between two characters, dark silhouette scenes, the recurring scale metaphor, or chart types (bar, line, pie, gauge). Those need a second test segment (see report).

measurement_method.boundaries: Hard cuts from ffmpeg scene filter (threshold 0.25) plus visual inspection of 1 fps labelled frames. The scene filter MISSES cuts between two light frames (for example cartoon to grey board), so some boundaries were set from frames at 1 s resolution (+/-0.5 s) and one (23.05 s) was verified at 10 fps. Boundaries marked boundary_confidence 'cut-detected' are +/-0.1 s; 'frame-estimated' are +/-0.5 s.
measurement_method.narration_times: Whisper base (int8, word timestamps) run on this segment's audio. Word times are the model's estimate (typically +/-0.3 s), not frame-measured.
measurement_method.narration_text_policy: The manifest stores a paraphrase of each shot's idea (narration_idea), not the narration text.
measurement_method.change_events: Hand-annotated from frames. Times are approximate (+/-1 s unless marked 'measured').
measurement_method.precision_warning: The reference is 640x360 H.264. Small text, mouth shapes and exact colours are low-confidence.

summary.whole_video_scene_changes_note: 283 (R1) and 318 (R2) detected changes at threshold 0.3 give a mean of 7.5 s per change, but this is a LOWER BOUND (the detector misses light-to-light cuts). In this segment the true shot rate is about one per 5.0 s.

shots.narration_idea: Introduces a town on the US-Mexico border by name.
shots.composition: Satellite view of North America; camera pushes from continental view down to the Arizona-Sonora border. Narrator standing at the right edge.

narrator.pose: standing, mouth open, arm toward content (arm detail low confidence)
narrator.scale: about one third of frame height

shots.continuity: Opens the Nogales thread; map returns at S11 and S13.

shots.narration_idea: Corrects the first impression: it is two towns.
shots.composition: Flat desert town: rows of adobe houses, cacti, road, sun and clouds. No fence yet.

change_events.what: two small labels typed over the two halves

shots.continuity: First appearance of the desert-town set (reused S04, S05, S07, S09).

shots.narration_idea: A fence runs through the middle of it.
shots.composition: Colour street-level photograph of a border street with a tall fence and patrol vehicles; city on a hill behind.
on_screen_text: the fence (small white typed key phrase, top)

change_events.what: key phrase typed over the photo

shots.continuity: Real photo used as proof right after the cartoon claim.

shots.narration_idea: North side is one named town, south side is the other, in a different country.
shots.composition: Same desert town, now with a wooden fence; camera slides right across it. US flag over left houses, Mexico flag over right houses.
shots.continuity: Colour roles begin: USA/north text blue-grey, Mexico/south text green.

shots.narration_idea: Same desert, same weather, same families with cousins on both sides.
shots.composition: Wide shot of the fenced town. A check-list types in at the top; a blue family on the left and a green family on the right appear and wave.
shots.continuity: Blue family = USA side, green family = Mexico side. Reused as thumbnails in S10.

shots.boundary_confidence: measured at 10 fps (start: hard cut between 23.00 and 23.10), cut-detected (end)
shots.narration_idea: The same food, the same music, often the same language.
shots.composition: Plain light-grey board. Narrator at left. Two column headers; three rows of paired round icons (blue-ringed USA, green-ringed Mexico) joined by an equals sign and a typed word.

narrator.pose: standing, one arm extended toward content

shots.transition_in: hard cut (measured: no blend frames at 10 fps)

change_events.what: first icon pair pops in, label typed (measured)

shots.continuity: Colour roles continue (blue USA / green Mexico). Narrator first appears in left-on-board placement.

shots.narration_idea: Sets up a comparison of a household on each side.
shots.composition: Same fenced desert town, both families standing.
shots.continuity: Fifth return to the desert-town set.

shots.narration_idea: A household on the American side earns about three times as much.
shots.composition: Grey board, narrator left. Two house icons separated by a fence post. Coin stacks grow beside each house; the USA stack is clearly taller. A dark navy tag shows the ratio.
shots.transition_in: hard cut (not verified at fine resolution)

change_events.what: one coin appears on each house

shots.continuity: Same two-column colour roles. The 'house + coins' pair returns in later boards (not inspected).

shots.narration_idea: People on the north side live longer, have better roads and safer streets.
shots.composition: Fenced desert town with both families; a tick list types in; the sky shifts from day to dusk across the shot.
shots.continuity: Time-of-day shift used as a mood beat. Last use of the full cartoon set in this segment.

shots.narration_idea: Same place, same people, completely different lives.
shots.composition: Grey board; narrator left; two framed thumbnails of the cartoon scene (blue frame USA, green frame Mexico); typed summary lines, the last in red.
key_objects: two framed thumbnails of earlier scene

narrator.pose: standing, arm extended, eyes open/closed alternate

shots.continuity: The earlier cartoon scene is re-used as a recap thumbnail: asset reuse as a story device.

shots.narration_idea: Zooms out: the USA is the richest big country; its southern neighbours are mostly middle-income.
shots.composition: Satellite globe view of the Americas. USA gets a translucent white fill and label with a yellow sub-line; camera pans south; Latin America tinted gold; country labels. Narrator at right for the first ~4 s, then not visible.
on_screen_text: richest big country in history (yellow sub-line)

narrator.scale: about one third of frame height
narrator.note: visible ~47-51 s, not visible ~52-58 s while the camera pans

shots.transition_in: hard cut (two cuts 0.5 s apart; the second may be a camera hop)

change_events.what: Latin America turns gold, Mexico label

shots.continuity: Establishes the map colour language: highlighted rich = white/blue, middle-income Latin America = gold.

shots.boundary_confidence: cut-detected; internal clear measured at 62.3 s (6.7 fps strip)
shots.narration_idea: Many struggle with poverty, inflation and crime; then 'but here is the twist'; it was not always like this.
shots.composition: Grey board, narrator left. Three white cards with orange border (house, banknote with rising arrow, red siren), each with a one-word label. At ~62.3 s the board clears; the outlined yellow display title scales in; a typed subtitle follows; a dark date chip shows a year that changes; a red typed line.
on_screen_text: a short red line meaning it was not always like this

narrator.pose: standing; mouth open/closed toggling about every 0.15-0.3 s; eyes blink (measured 62.0-65.0 s)

change_events.what: THE TWIST starts scaling in (measured onset 63.05, full size 63.2)
chip changes to 1700, red line typed

shots.continuity: The 'twist' title pops on its key word; the subtitle completes with the end of the sentence.

shots.narration_idea: Around 1700 the richest places in the Americas were in Latin America.
shots.composition: Satellite world view; small grey date chip top-left reading 1700; three gold coin pins appear on Latin American locations; yellow text; narrator at right.
on_screen_text: the north poor (small grey, at north)

narrator.pose: standing, mouth open; expression changes to a smile at ~73 s
narrator.scale: about one third of frame height

shots.narration_idea: Mexico City was a grand capital of around a hundred thousand people.
shots.composition: Full-frame colonial-era painting of a plaza and cathedral under a smoky sky; edges softly darkened or blurred to fill the 16:9 frame. White title, yellow subtitle, and a person icon with a counting number.
shots.continuity: Painting first, cartoon of the same subject next (S15): archival proof then cartoon explanation.

shots.narration_idea: The city had a university and a cathedral.
shots.composition: Cartoon Mexico City: cathedral with gold dome, volcano behind, a line of about 16 small characters along the bottom; a university building slides in.
shots.continuity: Crowd row = population device (reused S17).

shots.narration_idea: Boston at the time was a town of a few thousand.
shots.composition: Split screen with a thin black divider: Mexico City cartoon on the left, a small New England town (white church, two settlers, pines) on the right.

change_events.what: Boston panel appears on the right

shots.continuity: Size contrast shown by composition, not a chart.

shots.narration_idea: A silver-mining city in the mountains of Bolivia.
shots.composition: Huge red-brown cone mountain with dark mine openings and white silver dots; a long row of small characters along the bottom.
shots.continuity: Cartoon then archival of the same city (S18).

shots.narration_idea: One of the biggest cities in the world.
shots.composition: Dark red-brown bird's-eye historic painting of the city under the mountain, with a legend in the artwork's corner; slight slow zoom.
on_screen_text: one of the biggest cities in ... (white, typed)
shots.continuity: The cut lands mid-sentence on a key phrase, not at a sentence start.

shots.narration_idea: The Caribbean sugar islands were among the richest places on Earth.
shots.composition: Satellite zoom on the Caribbean; four yellow pins with labels; small sugar-cane icons beside them; white heading and yellow typed sub-heading. No narrator.
on_screen_text: some of the richest places on Earth (yellow)
shots.continuity: Gold typed text on map = the 'rich' reading of the south.

shots.narration_idea: The north was a poor, cold, empty backwater.
shots.composition: Snowy landscape: a lone settler near a log cabin among pines, light snowfall. Three words spaced across the top, then a single capitalised word.
shots.continuity: Contrast pair with S15-S17 (crowded rich south vs empty poor north).

shots.narration_idea: So what happened? How did the poor north become the richest while the rich south fell behind?
shots.composition: Grey board. Narrator large and centred-left for the first ~1 s with a yellow question mark, then small at left. '1700' and 'TODAY' column headers; blue box 'poor north' with a blue arrow growing to 'richest'; a yellow 'rich south' box with a red arrow crossing down to an orange 'fell behind' box.

narrator.pose: large with arms raised at 99.6-100.8 s, then small and standing
narrator.scale: large then about one third of frame height

change_events.what: blue arrow grows to richest box
rich south box and red crossing arrow to fell behind

shots.continuity: Colour roles: blue = poor north (rising), yellow/gold = rich south (falling). The same roles recur in S24 and in later boards (R2 sheets).

shots.narration_idea: To understand it, go back to the moment Europeans arrived.
shots.composition: Satellite view of the Atlantic; a small date chip (value low confidence, appears to read 1492); two white route lines from Europe toward the Caribbean; a red flag marker; narrator at right.

narrator.scale: about one third of frame height

shots.continuity: Date chip is the way the video steps back in time.

shots.narration_idea: ...and to a very strange lesson.
shots.composition: Grey board; narrator left changing from closed mouth to open to pointing; a cream scroll appears blank, then fills with a two-line title; a red '?!' burst at its corner.
shots.continuity: Scroll = chapter-title device (also seen elsewhere in R2).

shots.narration_idea: The worst thing that can happen to a country is to be born rich.
shots.composition: Grey board; narrator small at left; red typed line at top; a gold crown-treasure cradle labelled born rich appears, then a plain rough cradle labelled born poor; finally a red down arrow beside rich and a blue up arrow beside poor.

narrator.pose: small, standing, mouth closed then open
narrator.scale: about one quarter of frame height

shots.transition_in: hard cut or in-place clear (not verified)

change_events.what: down arrow on rich, up arrow on poor

shots.continuity: The paradox (rich falls, poor rises) is drawn with the same gold/blue roles as S21. This is the aphorism that the video keeps returning to.

recurring_elements.description: One straw-hat stick figure with a spear. Placed at the left on boards, at the right on maps, almost never in cartoon scenes. Present about half of this segment.
Blue = USA / north / poor-north; green = Mexico; gold or yellow = rich / south / treasure; red = emphasis, conclusion, loss. Held across cartoon, board and map in this segment.
One cartoon set used five times (S02, S04, S05, S07, S09) and re-used as a thumbnail (S10).
Short key phrases typed on screen in a handwritten face (dark on board, white or yellow on scenes and maps); a heavy outlined yellow display face for chapter-style titles.
A small rounded chip showing a year, used on maps and boards; the value can change in place (2009 to 1700).
NOT in this segment. In later parts of R2 the sticky note 'who gets to keep it' and a balance scale (south gold, north blue) recur; in R1, whale and shrimp. They need a second test segment.
